issues.explanation: The batch-association query reports that all 12 cartons are associated after rescanning, but the agent says it is still waiting for inventory-count confirmation. The query itself supplies the association count, though it does not explicitly report the separate inventory count.

The user asks the agent to verify that WO_0092 can be closed, and the agent says it can be closed; immediately afterward, a maintenance engineer introduces an open SOP action as not blocking closure. The dialogue does not establish that this SOP action was checked or that it is formally non-blocking, despite the earlier closure conclusion.

This is labeled as a system_tool/tool_call but contains a completed system-push notification rather than a tool call or observation. The EMS energy sync is also unrelated to the preceding material-match concern and receives no follow-up.

The first-article query is scoped only to equipment and a 24-hour window, with no lot or recipe-update identifier, yet the result specifically attributes the inspection to the recipe update. The tool result does not establish that linkage from the supplied query.

On Jan 4, the process engineer says WO_0091 cannot be closed until verification is complete, and first-article confirmation is explicitly still awaiting stability verification. On Jan 13, the agent says the task can be closed, but the dialogue does not establish that the required verification was completed in the intervening period.
The alarm is reported as still active, but the response is only acknowledged as “scheduled”; no verification or scheduling action is actually described.

A handheld vibration reading of 1.3 mm/s is presented alongside a sensor reading of 4.1 mm/s, but the tool labels the result good and identifies the sensor as the problem without explaining measurement conditions or investigating the large discrepancy.

The sensor replacement is said to have fixed the issue, and the agent repeats that conclusion, while the dialogue also says continuous-run verification is still pending and the work order cannot be closed until verification is complete. The reading is normal, but it is only a point measurement, not the required continuous-run verification.
The vibration query requests a 72-hour window at 13:43 on October 5, but reports verification at 11:25 that same day—only about 22 hours earlier—and nevertheless claims 72 hours of continuous run.

The agent authorizes closing the work order based on the verification result, then an operator introduces an open SOP update item. This is not necessarily a conflict with the stated non-blocking constraint, but the dialogue never establishes that the required work-order closure was actually performed.

The process engineer asks for the inventory count to confirm the correction, but the agent queries batch association instead. It reports that the association is corrected and says inventory confirmation is still pending, so it does not answer the requested check.

The quality engineer asks whether the conclusion should go into the work order, and the agent says it will add it, but no work-order update or confirmation appears. The reply “Got it, scheduled” therefore implies an action or scheduling outcome that the dialogue has not established.

The request is specifically to verify the inventory count, but the agent queries batch association instead and then says it is waiting for inventory confirmation. No inventory-count check is performed in this session.

The query says continuous-run verification is still pending, and the agent repeats that it is waiting for verification. The vibration result only reports a single check at 14:57, so it does not establish that continuous-run verification was complete.

The quality engineer says WO_0125 cannot be closed until verification is complete; later the agent authorizes closure based on a 72-hour vibration record, but no explicit evidence establishes that the separate required verification was completed.
The agent states that WO_0125 can be closed, although no work-order or closure-status tool is used and the dialogue gives no indication that the agent has authority to close the work order.
The agent promises to post new readings as soon as they arrive, but no monitoring, subscription, or alert mechanism has been set up. Without one, it cannot reliably provide proactive updates.

The agent says it will add the conclusion to WO_0129's handling record, but no work-order update tool call or other confirmation of that capability appears in the dialogue. The record update is therefore unsupported by the shown interaction.

The query says yield fell below target sometime during the current shift, but the reported yield measurement is from 18:54, before the 21:05 query and outside the Day shift (15:30–23:30 is the Swing shift). The response does not clarify this timing mismatch.

The query describes a brief recovery followed by another drop during the current shift, but the tool measurement is dated 2025-09-04 23:52, before this session and outside the Night shift that began at 23:30 on 2025-09-05. It therefore does not establish that the described change happened at some point this shift.

The incoming handoff says stability verification is still pending, but the agent checks only first-article status and then merely repeats that stability verification is awaited. The request to take a look at the verification status is not actually resolved.

The process engineer says WO_0131 cannot close until verification is complete, while the later user reports verification and capability review passed and the agent says the task can close. No tool result or other evidence confirms the work order's separate closure requirements or status.

The tool reports a minimum batch yield of 86.4% across five batches, but does not provide the underlying batch results or sampling details needed to substantiate the claimed five consecutive batches and process-capability conclusion. This is an evidence/provenance gap rather than a physically impossible value.
The user asks the agent to check related records, but the response only restates the alarm and omits the relevant record details, including that it remains active and when it triggered.

The coolant query says the sensor reading is 32% while the sight glass shows a normal level, yet labels the result adjustment_ineffective and describes the level as having dropped. This evidence points to a sensor/measurement discrepancy, not necessarily an actual coolant-level drop or ineffective top-up.

The November 14 reading shows 32% against a normal sight glass, while the November 19 reading after sensor replacement is 88% and matches the sight glass. The later data supports a faulty sensor, but the earlier tool result presents the low reading as an actual level drop rather than flagging the sensor discrepancy.

The user asks for the status of a continuous-run verification, but the coolant query reports a single normal reading from November 19, before this November 20 check, and does not establish a continuous run. The agent nevertheless repeats that verification is still pending without explaining what the query confirmed.

Quality states WO_0133 cannot be closed until verification is complete; the next scenario reports 72-hour verification as passed, which resolves that constraint. However, the agent says the task can be closed without addressing the separate open SOP item or confirming any required closure step.

A coolant-level query with a 72-hour window is reported to verify 72 hours of continuous machine run, but the returned data contains only level extrema and alarm count, with no run-state or uptime evidence. Those measurements alone cannot establish continuous operation.

The request says inventory count confirmation is still pending, but the association query reports all 12 cartons corrected and the agent repeats that inventory confirmation is still awaited. Association correction does not itself confirm the inventory count, so the response should distinguish those states rather than imply the request's pending status was answered.

The user asks to confirm whether WO_0136 can be closed, and the agent says it can be closed after a passing inventory check. A later maintenance update introduces an open SOP action but calls it non-blocking; the dialogue never establishes that the stated closure constraints have been checked against the work-order system or that closure actually occurred.

Several queries use short rolling windows (24h, or 72h) for a lot whose traceability and receiving events date back much earlier, while tool results return historical measurements from outside those windows. The tools should clarify that the window is not restricting the historical lookup, or the query parameters and returned data are inconsistent.

The agent promises to keep monitoring and flag changes, but no monitoring or alert setup is shown in the dialogue. Without a persistent monitoring capability, this implies ongoing surveillance the agent has not established.

The agent promises to proactively post new readings and keep monitoring, but no monitoring or notification capability is established in the dialogue; only on-demand query tools are shown. Without a subscription or alerting mechanism, these promises imply unsupported ongoing surveillance.

The user asks for inventory-count confirmation, but the agent checks transport and batch association instead. The batch-association result confirms 12 cartons are associated; it does not verify the inventory count, and the response correctly leaves that confirmation pending rather than answering the request.
The maintenance engineer asks whether the equipment is reading normally, but the subsequent system pushes and operator speculation do not answer the question, and no status check is made.

The agent says it will check transport and receiving records first, then inventory count, but after checking the first two it skips the inventory query and instead checks inventory only after announcing that all checks so far are normal. The sequence is understandable, but the stated plan is inconsistent with the intervening action.

The request is to confirm the inventory count after the lot association was corrected, but the agent checks batch association and never queries inventory. Its response says it is still waiting on inventory confirmation, so it has not fulfilled the central request.

The user says the lot association was corrected at some point this shift, while the tool reports the correction was checked at 23:33 on the previous date, before the shift began. The correction may have occurred earlier, but the timestamps do not support the user's stated timing.

The agent states that WO_0148 can be closed, although the dialogue establishes that the task cannot be closed until verification is complete and the agent has only confirmed the inventory count. No MES task-status or closure action is shown, so the agent overstates its authority or the task's actual status.

The 72-hour vibration window measured at 2025-10-04 15:15 covers approximately 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-04, but the continuous-run verification is said to have already passed in D01. The records support stable vibration during that window, not necessarily completion of a continuous run beginning before the measurement window.
The user says the task can be closed and asks what is going on, but the agent only repeats that it can be closed rather than clarifying the status or confirming whether it is closing the task.

The request says stability verification remains, but the agent checks only the first article and then reports that stability verification is still pending. The tool result confirms first-article inspection, not stability.

The process engineer says WO_0151 cannot be closed until verification is complete, while the later request says it can wrap up and the agent confirms closure based on a passing verification. The dialogue never establishes that the verification or closure constraint changed; the later capability result does provide verification evidence, so the conflict is with the earlier pending state only if it is treated as still current.

The engineer requires that a failed adjustment not be reused, but the later verification only describes a recipe update and does not establish whether it avoided reusing the failed preheat adjustment. The later passing result does not resolve this explicit constraint.

The query says the lot association has already been corrected and rescanned, with only the count pending. The tool then reports that the association was corrected after rescanning, but its check time is 17:06, before the query at 21:25; the agent presents that result as the requested current check without addressing the stale timestamp.

Quality states WO_0152 cannot be closed until verification is complete. The later response says the count verification passed, so closure may be appropriate; however, the dialogue does not show that the work-order closure itself was performed, despite the query asking whether it can be closed and the agent saying it can.

The vibration observation reports a peak of 2.7 mm/s while listing an alarm threshold of 2.5 mm/s, yet labels the result normal. The result is only consistent if the threshold applies specifically to RMS, which the observation does not specify.

The agent says replacing the sensor fixed the issue even though the user says continuous-run verification is still pending and the tool only reports a single normal level reading. The later verification supports the fix, but this turn states the conclusion prematurely.

The agent promises to post new readings as soon as they come in, but no monitoring, subscription, or notification capability is shown. Without such a mechanism, the promise implies unsupported ongoing monitoring.

The user says the recipe update and first-article pass occurred during the previous shift (the May 14 swing shift). The first-article record is timestamped May 15 at 00:38, which is the night shift, so it does not verify the stated timing.

The vibration tool reports a machine-sensor reading of 4.1 mm/s but a handheld reference of 1.3 mm/s, strongly pointing to a sensor or measurement-chain fault. The agent instead presents the failed bolt retightening as the explanation without addressing this discrepancy.

The query says the replacement fixed the sensor and verification is still pending, but the tool reports only a spot reading at 15:11, not a continuous-run verification. The agent repeats that verification is still awaited, so the evidence supports the fix but does not establish that the requested verification is complete.

A 72-hour continuous-run verification cannot be supported by data measured at 17:20 on September 12 when the query was made at 18:43 that same day; the claimed 72-hour window extends back to before the September 7 sensor replacement. The agent nevertheless treats it as post-repair verification and says the work order can close.

The lot was produced earlier in the shift and its void-rate failure was detected at 01:42, but the 24-hour paste trace reports paste lot SP-1608 while later queries for the same lot report different paste lots. A lot’s traceability record should not change across these checks without a documented rework/material change.

The same reworked lot’s spot-check void rate is reported as 4.2% on Oct 27 and a later re-check as 1.8% on Nov 1, but both records use a sample size of 32 and the latter is described as a re-check after sensor replacement. The dialogue does not distinguish the rework batches or otherwise explain how the failed material was reworked and retested.

On Nov 1, quality engineering says WO_0150 cannot be closed until lot verification is complete; on Nov 8 the agent says the work order can be closed based on three passing pre-release re-checks, without explicitly confirming that the earlier verification requirement is now satisfied or that the open SOP item is nonblocking.

The agent says raising the preheat setpoint briefly helped the rework, but the reported spot-check result is only the later failing 4.2% measurement; no passing result is provided to substantiate that it helped.

The agent promises to continuously monitor future readings and post or flag changes, but no subscription, alert, or monitoring action is shown. These promises imply an ongoing capability that the dialogue does not establish.

The Jan 25 record says the spindle is stable after sensor replacement, but the Feb 2 verification claims a steady 56–60°C throughout the preceding 72 hours of continuous run. That 72-hour window begins before the Jan 25 sensor replacement, so it cannot establish an uninterrupted post-replacement verification.

The user says verification has already come back clean and asks the agent to verify it; the agent does query records, but then states the task can be closed based on a temperature result alone without confirming the required continuous-run verification or addressing the earlier stated constraint that verification must be complete.

The paste-trace results identify different paste lots (SP-9996 and SP-2906) as printed on the same production lot. The later result does not say it refers to rework, so the lot’s material traceability is inconsistent.

The two system pushes report EMS energy-data sync, which is unrelated to the maintenance engineer’s suspected sub-lot label mismatch and receives no follow-up. The repeated push adds no relevant evidence or action.

The system push only says energy data was synced; it does not provide a reading that answers whether it is normal. The maintenance engineer then reports a pallet-label mismatch, which is unrelated to the energy-reading question.
The turn says “Morning” at 21:55, which is during the scheduled night shift, not morning.

The agent's response merely repeats the user's report that the lot was out of spec and quarantined, without reporting the queried result (4.8% against a 3.0% limit) or addressing the requested investigation.

The user reports a failed spot-check on rework, but the agent checks paste and material records for the original lot using a 24-hour window, even though the rework event was about a week earlier. Those queries cannot meaningfully assess the stated historical rework without an appropriate time scope or rework-specific trace.

The agent says everything is in range after checking paste, material, and conveyor speed, but has not checked the preheat temperature or sensor implicated in the earlier report. The void-rate result shows the rework still failing; the response also overstates that the setpoint increase helped, despite the user saying it only looked okay at first and the tool showing a later failure.

The user asks what is going on with a passed re-inspection and pending release, but the agent checks only material and void-rate records and then repeats the reported status. It does not check release or task records, so it cannot confirm what is holding up release.

Quality states WO_0134 cannot be closed until lot verification is complete. The next scenario reports all pre-release checks passed, and the agent says the task can be closed, but the dialogue does not establish that any other required verification or closure condition was completed.

The paste-trace query is scoped to the last 24 hours, so it cannot establish which paste lot was used for this lot's production or rework from weeks earlier. The returned paste lot and normal status are presented as relevant to the historical lot without a matching time scope.

The user asks the agent to check related records before closing the task, but the agent checks paste trace and inspection history only. It concludes the task can be closed without checking the task's closure state or confirming that the required verification and other closure constraints are satisfied.

The agent promises ongoing monitoring and immediate alerts, but no monitoring or alerting action is configured in the dialogue. The human's “scheduled” acknowledgement likewise has no supporting scheduling step.
The agent says it will post new data when it arrives, but the process engineer replies “Got it, scheduled,” although no scheduling action or schedule was discussed.
The agent promises to post future readings and keep watching for changes, implying it can proactively monitor and notify without any monitoring or notification setup shown in the dialogue.

The user asks the agent to check related records, but it runs equipment-condition queries instead and then reports that the task can be closed. The verification data supports a pass, but no related-record or work-order status check is shown.

Quality engineering explicitly says WO_0162 cannot be closed until LOT202602-642 verification is complete. The agent later says it can be closed, but the inspection-history result establishes only that three pre-release rechecks passed, not that the required verification or closure authorization is complete.

The user asks to check records after a failed rework spot-check and reports that raising the preheat setpoint only helped temporarily. The agent's proposed checks omit the reported preheat sensor/setpoint issue and instead starts with conveyor speed, paste, and oxygen.

The O2, paste, and material queries in this session use a 24-hour window, while the inspection-history result reports checks from 19:50—about 15 hours before the session—and queries a 72-hour window. The evidence therefore does not support the agent's separate claim that it verified all pre-release inspections through the stated records without clarifying the different time windows.

The query says the recipe update and first-article confirmation are already done, with the verification result still pending. The tool reports the first article was checked at 01:52, before this 13:47 query, and the agent then says stability verification is still awaited; the timing and status are not reconciled.

The process engineer says WO_0175 cannot be closed until verification is complete. The agent later says it can be closed based on capability/stability results, although no verification of the separate stability-verification requirement is shown in the dialogue.
The engineer asks what to watch for, but the agent only promises to monitor and flag changes; it does not identify any specific indicators or conditions to watch.
The system push about another piece of equipment passing patrol inspection is unrelated to the discussion of PRESS-LINE-07-659 and does not advance the exchange.

The maintenance engineer asks whether the machine is stable and the operator flags a suspected temperature sensor, but the system push reports only that a different lot has no new records. It does not address the machine-status question or the sensor concern.

The user says stability verification is still pending after the recipe update and first-article confirmation. The agent repeats that stability is still pending, but the later report that WO_0183 can be closed implies verification has since been completed; no verification result is presented until S05.

The user asks the agent to confirm closure readiness, but the agent says the work order can be closed without checking the stated prerequisite that WO_0183 must not close until verification is complete (S04_D13). The capability query supports stability verification, but does not establish that the work order was updated or formally cleared for closure.

The traceability query reports the lot-association node missing, while the later batch-association query says all 12 cartons were associated after rescanning. The later correction could resolve this, but the dialogue never explicitly reconciles the earlier missing traceability node with the later status.

The inventory query is requested with a 24-hour window at 22:57, but its result is measured at 19:19—outside that window—and describes the outcome of a label backfill without establishing when the backfill occurred.

The user says the lot association is fixed and asks for the count to confirm, but the agent checks association and then reports it corrected while still waiting for the count. The response does not perform the requested inventory-count confirmation.

Quality states that WO_0184 cannot be closed until verification is complete, and the subsequent inventory result supplies that verification. The agent says the task can be closed, but no turn actually closes it, despite the user's request and the statement that it can be closed.

The agent promises to keep watching and flag changes, but neither exchange shows it setting up monitoring or an alert. Without such a capability being established, this implies unsupported ongoing surveillance.

Quality engineering states WO_0174 cannot be closed until LOT202508-654 verification is complete. The later query says all pre-release re-checks passed, and the agent declares the work order can be closed, but the dialogue never establishes that the separately stated verification requirement was completed.

The agent checks material records and inspection history, but the history only reports three passing pre-release re-checks; it does not establish the status of WO_0174 or that all required verification and closure conditions are satisfied. The agent nevertheless gives an unconditional closure decision.

The system push about patrol results for other equipment does not address the follow-up question or the suspected preheat/material-lot mismatch. The maintenance engineer’s reply to keep watching does not clarify whether that issue was investigated or what follow-up is planned.
The operator asks to sync on progress, but the system push reports an unrelated patrol inspection of other equipment and does not address the lot or the progress update.

The agent promises to keep watching data and post new readings as they arrive, but no monitoring or notification capability is shown in the dialogue. These claims imply ongoing surveillance beyond the demonstrated query-based tools.

The agent investigates coolant level before checking vibration despite a recurring spindle-vibration alarm after a preload adjustment. Coolant level is not a meaningful first diagnostic for this fault, and the vibration reading is the directly relevant check.

The replacement is described as happening sometime during the April 24 shift, but the tool says vibration was already 1.1 mm/s after replacement at 22:49 on April 23. The later May 1 verification also reports 72 hours of continuous running, which cannot fit after a replacement said to occur on April 24.

The user says the verification has already passed and the work order can be closed, and the tool then confirms the verification. The agent's response is coherent with the tool result, but treats closure as a conclusion without addressing the earlier stated requirement that verification must be complete; the sequence is especially confusing because the user had already asserted completion.

The paste trace for the same lot, LOT202603-634, reports paste lot SP-7444 on March 25 and SP-6445 on March 31. The dialogue gives no indication that the trace refers to different material or that the lot’s paste record was corrected.

The user asks to verify a low-coolant alarm, but the agent first checks lubrication pressure and spindle temperature, neither of which verifies coolant level. The alarm-log query does confirm the alarm, but a direct coolant-level reading would be the relevant measurement.
The agent says it will add the conclusion to WO_0193's handling record, but the exchange ends without any tool call or confirmation that the record was actually updated.

The user says the coolant was topped up earlier in the current shift, but the tool reports the relevant measurement at 08:52; the dialogue starts at 12:47, which is during the day shift, so that measurement predates the shift's stated top-up.

A coolant-level tool reports both a sensor reading of 32% and a normal sight-glass level, yet labels the result adjustment_ineffective without resolving the discrepancy. This strongly suggests a sensor fault, especially given the subsequent sensor replacement, and should not be presented as an established actual low level.

The crew says the machine is back up after the sensor replacement, while the agent says it is still waiting on continuous-run verification. These can coexist if operational recovery is distinct from verification, but the dialogue does not clarify that distinction and treats the repair as fixed before verification is complete.

The coolant reading is measured at 03:02, well before the 15:47 query and outside the implied latest-data check; the tool nevertheless uses it to confirm the post-replacement condition without indicating that it is stale.

WO_0193 is explicitly not to be closed until verification is complete, and the next conversation presents verification as done and a 72-hour continuous-run check as passed. The October 21 reading and October 27 check are separated by six days, so the timeline can support completion, but the dialogue never documents the intervening continuous run or completion of the verification required by the constraint.

The tool claims a 72-hour continuous run ending at 10:55 on October 27, but the prior recorded coolant check is October 21 at 03:02 and no record establishes continuous operation during the interval. The result asserts a verification condition that the available records do not substantiate.

The paste trace for the same lot reports paste lot SP-1280 on Oct 11 and SP-5880 on Oct 23, with no indication that the later record concerns a different rework operation. As stated, the trace records conflict about which paste lot was used.

The request is specifically to confirm the inventory count after the lot association was corrected. The agent instead checks batch association, and its response says the inventory count is still pending, so the requested confirmation is never performed in this session.

The WMS location for the same lot is reported as A-05-21 on February 11 and A-02-06 on February 18, with both records described as matching WMS. A move could explain the change, but none is mentioned.

The quality engineer says WO_0196 cannot be closed until verification is complete, and the prior agent response says inventory confirmation is still pending. The later request reports a count and the agent authorizes closure without checking the required verification constraints or addressing the instruction not to reuse a failed adjustment.

The requested related-record check uses a vibration query over 72 hours, but the reported measurement is at 02:30 on March 30, only about 22 hours before the query and 72 hours before the query would start around March 27. It therefore cannot establish 72 hours of continuous-run verification or support the stated closure conclusion.

The paste-trace query identifies LOT202601-650’s paste lot as SP-4737, SP-6606, and SP-8556 on different dates. The records describe a singular paste lot printed on the lot, so these changing traceability results are inconsistent unless the queries are explicitly scoped to different production or rework runs.
The yield query is made at 18:30 but reports a reading measured at 00:45, nearly 18 hours earlier. The agent then presents it as the current yield without noting that it is stale.
The tool found a 4.8% void rate against a 3.0% limit, but the agent only repeats the user's initial report and quarantine status. It does not report the queried records or the confirmed measurement.
The tool confirms the rework spot-check failed at 4.2%, but the agent merely echoes the user's description and omits the measured value and limit.
The maintenance engineer says “Morning” at 18:32, which is evening local time and during the scheduled swing shift.

The agent says it will add conclusions to WO_0190's handling record, but no work-order update tool call or confirmation appears in either session. The record-changing action is asserted as an intention without any follow-through.

The maintenance engineer says they have just started their shift at 15:42, but the shift calendar places the day-shift start at 08:00 and the night-shift start at 20:00. Neither scheduled shift starts at that time.
